title.es: Club de lectura: la gran discusión

es: Debatir una historia en un club de lectura: proponer una lectura, defenderla con dos deducciones, conceder un punto y discrepar con educación.

teaching.en: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous on purpose, since the writer never says which version is true.
teaching.es: Yo sostendría que el final es ambiguo a propósito, ya que la autora nunca dice qué versión es la verdadera.
teaching.explanationEs: I would argue that… propone una lectura con prudencia; ambiguous admite más de una interpretación.
segments: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous on purpose,
since the writer never says which version is true.
teaching.audioText: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous on purpose, since the writer never says which version is true.

teaching.en: Some readers interpret the closed door as regret, yet a plausible reading is that she must have felt relieved.
teaching.es: Algunos lectores interpretan la puerta cerrada como arrepentimiento, pero una lectura verosímil es que ella tuvo que sentirse aliviada.
teaching.explanationEs: Plausible reading: una interpretación creíble según las pruebas; must have + participio deduce.
segments: Some readers interpret the closed door as regret, yet a
plausible reading is that she must have felt relieved.
teaching.audioText: Some readers interpret the closed door as regret, yet a plausible reading is that she must have felt relieved.

teaching.en: You can argue your view more strongly if you make a case for it with two clues from the text, not with feelings.
teaching.es: Puedes defender tu postura con más fuerza si la argumentas con dos pistas del texto, y no con sentimientos.
teaching.explanationEs: Make a case for + algo: defenderlo con pruebas ordenadas.
segments: You can argue your view more strongly if you make a case
for it with two clues from the text, not with feelings.
teaching.audioText: You can argue your view more strongly if you make a case for it with two clues from the text, not with feelings.

teaching.en: I take issue with that view; I am not convinced that the argument will hold water once we reread the last page.
teaching.es: Discrepo de ese punto de vista; no estoy convencido de que el argumento se sostenga cuando releamos la última página.
teaching.explanationEs: Take issue with es discrepar con firmeza; hold water, resistir una comprobación.
segments: I take issue with that view; I am not convinced that
the argument will hold water once we reread the last page.
teaching.audioText: I take issue with that view; I am not convinced that the argument will hold water once we reread the last page.

teaching.en: A fair debater will concede that a clue is strong and will not read too much into a single detail.
teaching.es: Quien debate con justicia admitirá que una pista es sólida y no le dará demasiada interpretación a un solo detalle.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede that… admite un punto sin cambiar de postura; read too much into, sobreinterpretar.
segments: A fair debater will concede that a clue is strong
and will not read too much into a single detail.
teaching.audioText: A fair debater will concede that a clue is strong and will not read too much into a single detail.

teaching.en: When two readers still argue after an hour, agree to disagree, or play devil's advocate to test your own view.
teaching.es: Cuando dos lectores todavía discuten después de una hora, conviene aceptar que se piensa distinto o hacer de abogado del diablo para poner a prueba la propia opinión.
teaching.explanationEs: Agree to disagree cierra un debate con respeto; play devil's advocate, defender lo contrario por método.
segments: When two readers still argue after an hour, agree to
disagree, or play devil's advocate to test your own view.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta admite un punto sin abandonar la propia lectura?

choices.text: I see your point, and I concede it, but I read the ending differently.
I concede everything you say, so I must have been wrong from the start.
That point is fair, which is exactly why your reading cannot be plausible.

feedback.es: Concede un punto concreto y mantiene su lectura con but; la que lo concede todo renuncia a su lectura y la que niega lo que admite se contradice.

hint.es: Busca la opción que reconoce el punto y, aun así, mantiene la propia lectura.

prompt.es: Completa: «Yo sostendría que ambas lecturas son verosímiles.»

feedback.es: I would argue that… es la fórmula prudente para proponer una lectura.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «sostener» y va seguido de that.

origin.text: Some readers say the narrator lied. Others say he was only afraid. I would ___ that both readings are plausible.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tendremos que aceptar que pensamos distinto sobre la última página.»

answer.text: We will have to agree to disagree about the last page

feedback.es: Agree to disagree cierra el debate con respeto, sin que nadie tenga que ceder.

hint.es: Empieza con We will have to y termina con about the last page.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige en qué discrepa la hablante.

choices.text: She agrees that he lied, but thinks the letter explains why.
She thinks being nervous is not solid proof that he lied.
She finds the letter a weaker clue than his being nervous.

feedback.es: Discrepa de que el nerviosismo sea prueba de mentira y propone la carta como pista más fiable; no acepta que mintiera.

origin.audio: I take issue with that reading. You say the narrator lied because he was nervous, but nervous people are not always liars. To my mind, the letter is the real clue. If she knew the truth, she must have hidden it, and he might have found it much later.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula del club de lectura con su función.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple un paso distinto del debate: proponer, discrepar, conceder y cerrar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese argumento no se sostiene cuando relees el primer capítulo.»

feedback.es: Hold water se usa para un argumento que resiste una comprobación.

origin.text: You say the narrator is lying because he is nervous. But that argument does not hold ___ once you reread the first chapter.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra Carlos al final de la discusión.

choices.text: He concedes Sara's point and quietly drops his accusation.
He hopes the suggestion will persuade Sara to change her mind.
He keeps his view but ends the debate politely.

feedback.es: Proponer aceptar el desacuerdo, sonriendo, y el narrador aclara que tampoco cambió de opinión: mantiene su postura y cierra con educación.

origin.audio: At the club, Carlos argued for an hour that the narrator was a liar. Sara listened, nodded at the right moments, and then said that he made a fair point about the letter, and that she would gladly concede it. What she could not accept, she said, was that one lie makes every page a lie. A reader who reads too much into one detail ends up writing a different novel. Carlos smiled, looked at the ceiling and suggested that they should agree to disagree, which, everyone understood, meant that he had not changed his mind either.

prompt.es: ¿Para qué dice la autora que hará de abogada del diablo?

choices.text: To test how well each reading is supported.
To push members to adopt her own reading of the ending.
To show that the ending has no plausible reading.

feedback.es: Dice que discrepará de cualquier postura para que cada miembro elija pistas sólidas; ella misma duda de su propia versión, así que no busca imponer la suya.

origin.text: Dear all, before Thursday, could you each send one piece of evidence for your reading of the ending? I will play devil's advocate at the meeting: whatever you argue, I will take issue with it, so please choose clues that can hold water. I am not entirely convinced by any version so far, including my own.

prompt.es: Completa: «Debo admitir que la última línea lo apoya, pero el resto del libro no.»

feedback.es: Concede that… admite un punto del otro sin renunciar a la propia lectura.

origin.text: Tom says the ending is a happy one. I must ___ that the last line supports him, but the rest of the book does not.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: lectura, dos deducciones, concesión y cierre respetuoso.

answer.text: I would argue that the ending of The Blue Door is ambiguous on purpose. The narrator says that nobody ever lived in the house, but he can't have been honest, because he also says that his sister left after an argument. The wet letter is a clue: she must have been upset when she wrote it, and he might have kept it hidden for years. A plausible reading is that the blue door is a symbol of a memory that he cannot close. Carlos argues that the narrator is simply lying to us, and I concede that this is possible. However, I take issue with the idea that one lie spoils the whole book, and I am not entirely convinced that the writer wants us to be certain. But we should not read too much into one lie. The imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate, and the ending stays open to interpretation. We will have to agree to disagree, Carlos.
accepted: I would argue that the ending of The Blue Door is ambiguous on purpose. The narrator says that nobody ever lived in the house, but he can't have been honest, because he also says that his sister left after an argument. The wet letter is a clue: she must have been upset when she wrote it, and he might have kept it hidden for years. A plausible reading is that the blue door is a symbol of a memory that he cannot close. Carlos argues that the narrator is simply lying to us, and I concede that this is possible. However, I take issue with the idea that one lie spoils the whole book, and I am not entirely convinced that the writer wants us to be certain. But we should not read too much into one lie. The imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate, and the ending stays open to interpretation. We will have to agree to disagree, Carlos.

In my reading, the last scene is ambiguous, and the blue door is a symbol of memory. The narrator can't have been telling the whole truth, because the letter was wet, so somebody must have read it or hidden it. His sister might have left in anger, and he might have closed the door to forget her. Carlos says that the narrator is lying, and I concede that this is plausible, because the clues contradict him. Even so, I am not convinced that the writer wants a clear answer, and I think it is wrong to read too much into one detail. The cold imagery conveys sadness, and the ending will resonate with anyone who has lost someone. You make a fair point, Carlos, but we will have to agree to disagree.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención propone una lectura, la apoya con dos deducciones, admite el punto del otro, discrepa con tacto y cierra con respeto.

origin.text: Club de lectura. La novela «The Blue Door» termina así: el narrador cierra la puerta azul de la casa y dice «Nobody ever lived here». Antes contó que su hermana se fue tras una discusión y que la carta de ella apareció mojada. Carlos cree que el narrador miente. Escribe tu intervención (al menos 135 palabras; ideal, 220): propón tu lectura, defiéndela con dos deducciones, concede un punto, discrepa con tacto y cierra con respeto.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la autora de este mensaje tras el debate?

choices.text: She now doubts every reading, including the other members'.
She keeps her view but admits some doubt.
She is annoyed that nobody agreed with her.

feedback.es: No cambia su lectura, pero reconoce que el asunto es menos simple de lo que sostenía: mantiene su postura con una duda.

origin.text: Thank you all for a lively evening. I must have sounded stubborn, and I might have been; in fact, I went home and read the last chapter again, and I can't say that I am still certain. I am not ready to change my reading, but I am ready to admit that the matter is less simple than I claimed.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es fácil darle demasiada interpretación a un solo detalle.»

answer.text: It is easy to read too much into a single detail

feedback.es: Read too much into + algo describe sobreinterpretar un detalle aislado.

prompt.es: Concede un punto, pero mantén tu lectura.

answer.text: I concede that your reading is plausible, but I still find the ending ambiguous.
accepted: I concede that your reading is plausible, but I still find the ending ambiguous.
I admit that it is possible, but I would argue that the ending is open to interpretation.

feedback.es: Se concede el punto con I concede that y se mantiene la lectura con but.

origin.text: Un compañero dice que el narrador miente. Tú admites que es verosímil, pero sigues pensando que el final es ambiguo.
